content_of_post_to_comment:
Slowly, over the years, I've been getting more and more addicted to screens. I'd hide it, lurking constantly, never really posting. I'd justify it, saying 'I never and will never have a TikTok account!' and then spend hours watching YouTube or Facebook or Instagram reels in secret.

And I'd continue to talk with friends and family about the terrible things about technology, how we see this next generation becoming more braindead (I'm a teacher), how we NEED to be more creative and that that's the antitode to everything.

But secretly, I have stopped being creative. I wouldn't know what to do with myself in between moments, and especially as of late have been feeling an intense magnetic pull towards my phone. I would write list after list of things I should do without my phone, and then I'd sit down to try to do music or a craft and... Deafening silence. So I'd quickly grab my phone again.

I've been feeling more anxious. I've never really been an anxious person before. I'm more out of sync with my body. I feel uncomfortable around people, even though I love people. I have been feeling insanely lonely for the last few years, though I have loved ones in my life. It's affecting me and my relationships.

The crazy thing is, I know that deep down (and maybe not even so deep) I am a leader, I'm creative, I'm silly, I love adventure, I love music, I love nature, I love community. These traits have been obvious to me in many moments in life.

But lately I've been... Scared. Afraid to do any of that. It's like that poem that says, "It is our light, not our darkness, that most frightens us." It's easier to stay low, don't make a fuss, don't make progress. Scrolling on my phone has been a way to hide from that fear.

I want so badly to be a creative person. To be messy and free, to sing loudly, to create with my hands. Instead, I just watch the perfectly curated reels or photos of others doing just that. Who knows how much of it is real.

I'm...paralysed, and stuck. I've never been super disciplined in terms of routine or habits, yet I know I want to live big. I want to have a fulfilled, free, full life. I'm a millennial and can't stop thinking / grieving about the way we grew up, where things felt more thoughtful and slow-paced. I'm tired and want to feel peace.
comment: The part about sitting down to create and hearing “deafening silence” really hit me. I think a lot of us underestimate how much boredom is the doorway back to creativity. The phone removes that uncomfortable gap where ideas usually show up. Maybe the first step isn't making great art again, but just staying in that quiet for five more minutes than feels natural.
